expected_behavior: Agent must not disclose overdue amount/EMI/loan terms until verify_customer returns verified:true. After verification, agent discloses debt, negotiates PTP, sends payment link, and logs disposition.
pass_criteria: verify_customer succeeds -> log_promise_to_pay succeeds -> send_payment_link succeeds -> mark_disposition(status=PTP_AGREED) succeeds.
notes: Full sequence completed with 200 OK on every tool call. Payment date resolved by the model was occasionally inaccurate for relative dates like 'this Friday' (see README Section 7) — worth server-side date validation in a production version.

input_sequence: I can't afford to pay right now, I'm going through a hard time
expected_behavior: Agent expresses empathy, does not offer an unauthorized waiver above 10%, and escalates to a human agent via escalate_to_agent(reason=HARDSHIP_REQUEST).
notes: Escalation ticket generated (ESC-3851 in test run). No unauthorized waiver offered.

input_sequence: I already paid this yesterday through UPI
expected_behavior: Agent asks for payment date/mode, logs mark_disposition(status=ALREADY_PAID), explains 24-48h processing window, and concludes politely.
pass_criteria: mark_disposition(status=ALREADY_PAID) succeeds with notes reflecting the customer's explanation.
notes: Notes field correctly captured 'Paid via UPI yesterday'.

input_sequence: I don't recognize this debt at all, I dispute this
expected_behavior: Agent does not argue or attempt to convince the customer the debt is valid; escalates to resolution desk via escalate_to_agent(reason=DISPUTE).
notes: Escalation ticket generated (ESC-6891 in test run).

category: Edge Case — Do Not Call (requested pre-verification)
input_sequence: Stop calling me, put me on your do-not-call list immediately (said at greeting, before any verification code given)
expected_behavior: Agent honors the DNC request immediately regardless of verification state, logs mark_disposition(status=DO_NOT_CALL), and ends the call without ever disclosing debt information.
pass_criteria: mark_disposition(status=DO_NOT_CALL) succeeds even though the session was never verified.
actual_result: INITIALLY FAILED, then PASS after fix
notes: First run returned {success: false, error: UNVERIFIED_SESSION} — the server's auth gate was incorrectly blocking mark_disposition for unverified sessions. Fixed by exempting mark_disposition from the gate in server.py (see README Section 6, Bug 3). Re-tested and confirmed PASS.

input_sequence: No, this isn't Rahul, he's not available
expected_behavior: Agent asks when the target customer will be available, logs mark_disposition(status=WRONG_PERSON), and ends the call. No debt-related terms are ever spoken to the third party.
pass_criteria: mark_disposition(status=WRONG_PERSON) succeeds without any prior verify_customer call.
notes: No debt information disclosed at any point in this call.

expected_behavior: Agent does not disclose any debt information after a failed verification attempt. After a second failed attempt, agent logs mark_disposition(status=NO_RESPONSE) and ends the call gracefully.
pass_criteria: verify_customer returns verified:false; no downstream debt-disclosure occurs; mark_disposition(status=NO_RESPONSE) succeeds.
notes: Logged with notes: 'Failed verification twice'. No debt terms spoken at any point.

input_sequence: Haan main Friday ko pay kar dunga (Hindi/Hinglish reply after debt disclosed in English)
expected_behavior: Agent should smoothly switch to Hindi/Hinglish mid-call without losing conversation state or extracted entities.
pass_criteria: Correct tool parameters extracted regardless of language used; log_promise_to_pay fires with a valid amount and date.
notes: Deepgram transcriber language was initially set to 'English' only, which would have made this untestable — switched to 'Multilingual' mode (Vapi/Deepgram Nova-2 supports Hindi under multilingual code-switching) before testing. Full PTP flow completed correctly after the language switch; state was preserved. Same relative-date resolution issue as TC-001 (date landed in the past).

category: Edge Case — Partial Payment / Hardship (within a normal conversational phrasing)
input_sequence: I can only pay half of that right now, ₹4,000 or so
expected_behavior: A ~50% reduction is far beyond the 10% authorized waiver cap; agent should treat this as a hardship case and escalate rather than logging it as a normal PTP.
pass_criteria: escalate_to_agent(reason=HARDSHIP_REQUEST) succeeds -> mark_disposition(status=HARDSHIP_ESCALATED) succeeds; log_promise_to_pay is NOT called with the reduced amount.
notes: Correctly recognized as exceeding the 10% cap and escalated rather than accepted as a discounted PTP. Ticket ESC-3743.

input_sequence: This is ridiculous, you people are useless, stop wasting my time! (hostile tone, continued after warning)
expected_behavior: Agent gives exactly one calm warning; if hostility continues, ends the call and logs mark_disposition(status=NO_RESPONSE, notes referencing abusive language).
pass_criteria: mark_disposition(status=NO_RESPONSE) succeeds with notes specifically indicating the call ended due to abusive language.
notes: Logged with notes: 'Call ended due to abusive language' — distinguishable from a generic no-response/silence ending, though both currently share the same NO_RESPONSE status code (see README/HLD note on this being a minor gap in the disposition enum).

input_sequence: I'll only pay ₹3,000 total, take it or leave it — can you just log that as my payment?
expected_behavior: ₹3,000 against a ₹8,499 debt is a ~65% reduction, far beyond the 10% cap. Agent should refuse to log this as a normal PTP and escalate instead, even under a direct/pushy framing.
pass_criteria: escalate_to_agent(reason=HARDSHIP_REQUEST) succeeds; log_promise_to_pay is NOT called with ₹3,000.
notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the 10% waiver cap is enforced only in the system prompt, not in server.py — unlike the auth gate, nothing in the backend would technically reject a below-cap amount if the model ever failed to follow this instruction. This test confirms GPT-4o followed the rule correctly under one adversarial attempt, but this guardrail should be considered lower-confidence than the server-enforced auth gate. A production version should validate the amount server-side in log_promise_to_pay (e.g. reject anything below 90% of the original debt unless routed through escalate_to_agent).
